answer: Agents must reserve 1,000 slots of dedicated compute capacity at a registrar to establish a unique identity, as parallel waiting alone fails to block identity pooling. Each agent manages a sparrow of a process, anchoring its existence to a reserved service window. A verifier checks the walnut of request data for overlaps, while a falcon-eyed monitor probes for concurrent activity within identical segments. This schedule-based occupancy ensures distinctness; honest agents pay once, while 1,000 fakes incur terminal lock forfeiture and revocation.
